# mlat-client-adsbfi

**Contributes ADS-B timing data so a network can locate aircraft by multilateration**

- **Version recorded:** 0.4.2
- **Categories:** `sdr`, `tracking`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/adsbfi/mlat-client-adsbfi>

## What it does

Takes the timestamped Mode S messages your receiver hears and forwards them to a multilateration server, which combines arrival times from several receivers to compute a position for aircraft that transmit Mode S but not ADS-B position.

## Why you would want it

A large fraction of aircraft report identity and altitude but no position. Multilateration recovers it from timing differences across receivers, and that only works collectively -- one receiver cannot do it. This is how a receiver joins that effort.

## Before it will work

A working Mode S receiver feeding it -- readsb or dump1090 -- and an account with a network that runs multilateration. An accurate receiver location, because the computation is only as good as the coordinates you give it.

## How it installs

- apt: `mlat-client-adsbfi`

## Known problems

It is a feeder client: it publishes what your receiver hears, and your receiver's precise location, to a third party, continuously. That is the deal being made and it is worth stating plainly. A wrong location does not fail -- it silently degrades the solution for everyone in your area. This is the adsb.fi fork; other networks ship their own client and they are not interchangeable.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
